newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac calls for French youth jobs "crusade".
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls for French youth jobs "crusade".

text.p: President Jacques Chirac called on Monday for a "crusade" in 1997 to create jobs for French youths, a quarter of whom aged under 25 are jobless.

"I want 1997 to be the year in which real progress will be made on youth employment...a real crusade for the employment of youths," said Chirac, visiting a cyberspace centre for youths in a Paris suburb.
The French youth unemployment rate is more than double the national 12.7 percent unemployment rate, one of the highest in the European Union.
Chirac praised the cyber centre's facilities for youths to seek jobs through computer services and said the government would set up 20 such centres before the end of the year.

He called for a "change in mentalities" in tradition-bound France, saying more school-leaving youths should seek to enter apprenticeship programmes enabling them to have practical experience before seeking full-time jobs.

Chirac appeared on Sunday to encourage youths to seek experience aboard when he said in a newspaper interview: "Three million Germans, 4.3 million Italians and only 1.7 million French people work abroad. It's a wonder we are able to export so much despite lagging behind."
